week.description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents

week.description: Auto Ontology is a Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over data. It enables deterministic query generation, better context retrieval, and more explainable AI for LLM and agent workflows.
week.readme: Agents can retrieve documents and query databases, but reliability gates agentic analytics: a revenue metric answered faster is worth nothing if the number is wrong. Agents need a context layer that tells them where data lives, what it means, whether to use it, how to use it, where it came from, and what is similar. NVIDIA Auto Ontology is an open library that builds that layer from enterprise metadata, reconciles definitions across systems, and exposes it to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API.

week.description: Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact. A general purpose physics simulator.
week.readme: MuJoCo stands for Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact. It is a general purpose physics engine that aims to facilitate research and development in robotics, biomechanics, graphics and animation, machine learning, and other areas which demand fast and accurate simulation of articulated structures interacting with their environment. This repository is maintained by Google DeepMind. MuJoCo has a C API and is intended for researchers and developers.

week.description: Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory.
week.readme: My agent skills that I use every day to do real engineering - not vibe coding. Developing real applications is hard. Approaches like GSD, BMAD, and Spec-Kit try to help by owning the process. But while doing so, they take away your control and make bugs in the process hard to resolve. These skills are designed to be small, easy to adapt, and composable. They work with any model. They're based on decades of engineering experience. Hack around with them. Make them your own. Enjoy.

week.description: Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents.
week.readme: Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents. Skills encode the workflows, quality gates, and best practices that senior engineers use when building software. These ones are packaged so AI agents follow them consistently across every phase of development. 9 slash commands that map to the development lifecycle. Each one activates the right skills automatically. In Claude Code these install as plugin commands.

week.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings

It reads the accessibility tree of a desktop app and returns it as JSON, with a ref for every element the agent can act on. The agent clicks or types on a ref, reads the UI again to check the result, and repeats. The loop lives in your agent; agent-desktop has no model inside. It ships as a CLI and a C library.

items.title: Shared agent skills become dependable team standards once they survive compaction
items.connection: Matt Pocock's agent skills show demand for shared skills, and Kiro now reloads requested skills after compaction and lets users set when compaction starts, so a team skill no longer silently drops out of long runs.
items.context: engineering teams want consistent conventions across developers, and long agent sessions are where instructions get lost
chain: Skills were popular but fragile, because compaction could strip them out halfway through a long task.
Kiro reloading skills and steering files after compaction, plus a user-set threshold, makes their presence predictable.
A devex team can treat a curated skill set as an enforced standard, like a linter config, rather than a hint.
Onboarding and code consistency improve because new hires' agents follow the same team skills on day one.
items.who: Developer experience and platform teams at software companies; engineering leadership pays through tooling budget.
items.variable: share of long agent sessions that still follow team conventions at the end
items.versus: Without reload, teams must re-paste instructions by hand, and buying a new harness just to fix this costs far more than adopting a setting.
items.smallest_test: Run 20 long Kiro tasks with a team skill installed, with and without the new reload behavior, and count success if convention violations after compaction drop by half.
items.disconfirm: Sessions with reload still drift from the skill after compaction at about the same rate as before.

items.connection: Inkling 2 Small reads images and text under Apache 2.0, and Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe turns speech into text under Apache 2.0, so an inspector's photos and spoken notes can become a report without a cloud API.
items.context: insurers and property inspectors often cannot send client photos and recordings to third-party APIs
chain: Two permissively licensed models now cover the two inputs field staff actually produce: photos and voice.
Transcribed notes plus image descriptions can be merged into a draft report on an office server.
Firms that were blocked by data rules can automate report drafting, which shortens time from site visit to report.
Faster reports mean claims and inspections close sooner, which shifts staffing from typing to checking.
items.who: Insurance adjusters, property inspection and facilities firms; operations managers pay per seat or per report.
items.variable: hours from site visit to submitted report
items.versus: Cloud tools are off limits under many client contracts, and doing nothing leaves inspectors writing reports by hand.
items.smallest_test: Run 20 past inspections through the two-model pipeline and count success if inspectors accept at least 15 drafts with only light edits.
items.disconfirm: Inspectors rewrite most drafts because image descriptions or transcripts miss key details.

items.context: security and compliance reviews in insurers and banks usually demand cost control, audit logs and access control before any AI rollout
chain: Three separate gaps close on the same day: cost per user, a log of who called which tool, and login on MCP endpoints of internal Gradio apps.
A platform team can assemble a reviewable package from AWS-native and open parts instead of writing its own controls.
Security review shifts from blocking on missing controls to checking a known reference build, so approval moves faster.
Internal Gradio tools built by analysts can safely become agent tools, widening what agents can do inside the firm.

items.variable: weeks from pilot request to security approval
items.versus: Doing nothing leaves agents stuck in pilot, and buying a managed gateway still leaves internal MCP tools and tool-call audit unsolved.
items.smallest_test: Stand up the gateway, route one team's Kiro use in us-east-1 or eu-central-1, protect one internal Gradio tool with auth, and count success if the security team signs off on a 30-day pilot from that package alone.
items.disconfirm: Reviewers still reject it because CloudTrail covers only two regions or the reference build lacks controls they require.
